00.L1:
<n>1:1</n> Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, † et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
<n>1:2</n> Sed in lege Dómini volúntas ejus, * et in lege ejus meditábitur die ac nocte.
<n>1:4</n> Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
<n>1:5</n> Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in judício: * neque peccatóres in concílio justórum.
<n>1:6</n> Quóniam novit Dóminus viam justórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
00.L2:
<n>2:1</n> Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
<n>2:2</n> Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
<n>2:3</n> Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis jugum ipsórum.
<n>2:4</n> Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
<n>2:5</n> Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
<n>2:6</n> Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, * prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
<n>2:7</n> Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
<n>2:8</n> Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
<n>2:9</n> Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
<n>2:10</n> Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui judicátis terram.
<n>2:11</n> Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
<n>2:12</n> Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via justa.
<n>2:13</n> Cum exárserit in brevi ira ejus: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
00.L3:
<n>3:2</n> Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
<n>3:3</n> Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo ejus.
<n>3:4</n> Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
<n>3:5</n> Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
<n>3:6</n> Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
<n>3:7</n> Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
<n>3:8</n> Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
<n>3:9</n> Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
00.L6:
<n>6:2</n> Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
<n>6:3</n> Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam infírmus sum: * sana me, Dómine, quóniam conturbáta sunt ossa mea.
<n>6:4</n> Et ánima mea turbáta est valde: * sed tu, Dómine, úsquequo?
<n>6:5</n> Convértere, Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: * salvum me fac propter misericórdiam tuam.
<n>6:6</n> Quóniam non est in morte qui memor sit tui: * in inférno autem quis confitébitur tibi?
<n>6:7</n> Laborávi in gémitu meo, † lavábo per síngulas noctes lectum meum: * lácrimis meis stratum meum rigábo.
<n>6:8</n> Turbátus est a furóre óculus meus: * inveterávi inter omnes inimícos meos.
<n>6:9</n> Discédite a me, omnes, qui operámini iniquitátem: * quóniam exaudívit Dóminus vocem fletus mei.
<n>6:10</n> Exaudívit Dóminus deprecatiónem meam, * Dóminus oratiónem meam suscépit.
<n>6:11</n> Erubéscant, et conturbéntur veheménter omnes inimíci mei: * convertántur et erubéscant valde velóciter.
00.L7:
<n>7:2</n> Dómine, Deus meus, in te sperávi: * salvum me fac ex ómnibus persequéntibus me, et líbera me.
<n>7:3</n> Nequándo rápiat ut leo ánimam meam, * dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
<n>7:4</n> Dómine, Deus meus, si feci istud, * si est iníquitas in mánibus meis:
<n>7:5</n> Si réddidi retribuéntibus mihi mala, * décidam mérito ab inimícis meis inánis.
<n>7:6</n> Persequátur inimícus ánimam meam, † et comprehéndat, et concúlcet in terra vitam meam, * et glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat.
<n>7:10</n> Consumétur nequítia peccatórum, et díriges justum, * scrutans corda et renes, Deus.
<n>7:11</n> Justum adjutórium meum a Dómino, * qui salvos facit rectos corde.
<n>7:12</n> Deus judex justus, fortis, et pátiens: * numquid iráscitur per síngulos dies?
<n>7:13</n> Nisi convérsi fuéritis, gládium suum vibrábit: * arcum suum teténdit, et parávit illum.
<n>7:14</n> Et in eo parávit vasa mortis: * sagíttas suas ardéntibus effécit.
<n>7:15</n> Ecce, partúriit injustítiam: * concépit dolórem, et péperit iniquitátem.
<n>7:16</n> Lacum apéruit, et effódit eum: * et íncidit in fóveam quam fecit.
<n>7:17</n> Convertétur dolor ejus in caput ejus: * et in vérticem ipsíus iníquitas ejus descéndet.
<n>7:18</n> Confitébor Dómino secúndum justítiam ejus: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
00.L8:
<n>8:3</n> Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
<n>8:4</n> Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
<n>8:5</n> Quid est homo quod memor es ejus? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
<n>8:6</n> Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, † glória et honóre coronásti eum: * (7) et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
<n>8:8</n> Ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
<n>8:9</n> Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
<n>8:10</n> Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
00.L9:
<n>9:2</n> Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * narrábo ómnia mirabília tua.
<n>9:3</n> Lætábor et exsultábo in te: * psallam nómini tuo, Altíssime.
<n>9:4</n> In converténdo inimícum meum retrórsum: * infirmabúntur, et períbunt a fácie tua.
<n>9:5</n> Quóniam fecísti judícium meum et causam meam: * sedísti super thronum, qui júdicas justítiam.
<n>9:6</n> Increpásti gentes, et périit ímpius: * nomen eórum delésti in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>9:10</n> Et factus est Dóminus refúgium páuperi: * adjútor in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne.
<n>9:11</n> Et sperent in te qui novérunt nomen tuum: * quóniam non dereliquísti quæréntes te, Dómine.
<n>9:12</n> Psállite Dómino, qui hábitat in Sion: * annuntiáte inter gentes stúdia ejus:
<n>9:13</n> Quóniam requírens sánguinem eórum recordátus est: * non est oblítus clamórem páuperum.
<n>9:14</n> Miserére mei, Dómine: * vide humilitátem meam de inimícis meis.
<n>9:15</n> Qui exáltas me de portis mortis, * ut annúntiem omnes laudatiónes tuas in portis fíliæ Sion.
<n>9:17</n> Cognoscétur Dóminus judícia fáciens: * in opéribus mánuum suárum comprehénsus est peccátor.
<n>9:18</n> Convertántur peccatóres in inférnum, * omnes gentes quæ obliviscúntur Deum.
<n>9:19</n> Quóniam non in finem oblívio erit páuperis: * patiéntia páuperum non períbit in finem.
<n>9:20</n> Exsúrge, Dómine, non confortétur homo: * judicéntur gentes in conspéctu tuo.
<n>9:21</n> Constítue, Dómine, legislatórem super eos: * ut sciant gentes quóniam hómines sunt.
<n>9:22</n> Ut quid, Dómine, recessísti longe, * déspicis in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne?
<n>9:23</n> Dum supérbit ímpius, incénditur pauper: * comprehendúntur in consíliis quibus cógitant.
<n>9:24</n> Quóniam laudátur peccátor in desidériis ánimæ suæ: * et iníquus benedícitur.
<n>9:25</n> Exacerbávit Dóminum peccátor, * secúndum multitúdinem iræ suæ non quæret.
<n>9:27</n> Dixit enim in corde suo: * Non movébor a generatióne in generatiónem sine malo.
<n>9:28</n> Cujus maledictióne os plenum est, et amaritúdine, et dolo: * sub lingua ejus labor et dolor.
<n>9:29</n> Sedet in insídiis cum divítibus in occúltis: * ut interfíciat innocéntem.
<n>9:31</n> In láqueo suo humiliábit eum: * inclinábit se, et cadet, cum dominátus fúerit páuperum.
<n>9:32</n> Dixit enim in corde suo: Oblítus est Deus, * avértit fáciem suam ne vídeat in finem.
<n>9:33</n> Exsúrge, Dómine Deus, exaltétur manus tua: * ne obliviscáris páuperum.
<n>9:34</n> Propter quid irritávit ímpius Deum? * dixit enim in corde suo: Non requíret.
<n>9:36</n> Cóntere brácchium peccatóris et malígni: * quærétur peccátum illíus, et non inveniétur.
<n>9:37</n> Dóminus regnábit in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * períbitis, gentes, de terra illíus.
<n>9:38</n> Desidérium páuperum exaudívit Dóminus: * præparatiónem cordis eórum audívit auris tua.
<n>9:39</n> Judicáre pupíllo et húmili, * ut non appónat ultra magnificáre se homo super terram.
00.E1:
<n>1:1</n> Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, † nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.
<n>1:2</n> But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.
<n>1:4</n> Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.
<n>1:5</n> Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.
<n>1:6</n> For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.
00.E2:
<n>2:1</n> Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?
<n>2:2</n> The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.
<n>2:3</n> Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.
<n>2:4</n> He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.
<n>2:5</n> Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.
<n>2:6</n> But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.
<n>2:7</n> The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.
<n>2:8</n> Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.
<n>2:9</n> Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.
<n>2:10</n> And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.
<n>2:11</n> Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.
<n>2:12</n> Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.
<n>2:13</n> When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.
00.E3:
<n>3:2</n> Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.
<n>3:3</n> Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.
<n>3:4</n> But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.
<n>3:5</n> I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.
<n>3:6</n> I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.
<n>3:7</n> I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.
<n>3:8</n> For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.
<n>3:9</n> Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.
00.E6:
<n>6:2</n> Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation, * nor chastise me in thy wrath.
<n>6:3</n> Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak: * heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled.
<n>6:4</n> And my soul is troubled exceedingly: * but thou, O Lord, how long?
<n>6:5</n> Turn to me, O Lord, and deliver my soul: * O save me for thy mercy’s sake.
<n>6:6</n> For there is no one in death, that is mindful of thee: * and who shall confess to thee in hell?
<n>6:7</n> I have laboured in my groanings, † every night I will wash my bed: * I will water my couch with my tears.
<n>6:8</n> My eye is troubled through indignation: * I have grown old amongst all my enemies.
<n>6:9</n> Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity: * for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.
<n>6:10</n> The Lord hath heard my supplication: * the Lord hath received my prayer.
<n>6:11</n> Let all my enemies be ashamed, and be very much troubled: * let them be turned back, and be ashamed very speedily.
00.E7:
<n>7:2</n> O Lord my God, in thee have I put my trust: * save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.
<n>7:3</n> Lest at any time he seize upon my soul like a lion, * while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save.
<n>7:4</n> O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, * if there be iniquity in my hands:
<n>7:5</n> If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, * let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies.
<n>7:6</n> Let the enemy pursue my soul, † and take it, and tread down my life on the earth, * and bring down my glory to the dust.
<n>7:10</n> The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to nought: and thou shalt direct the just: * the searcher of hearts and reins is God.
<n>7:11</n> Just is my help from the Lord: * who saveth the upright of heart.
<n>7:12</n> God is a just judge, strong and patient: * is he angry every day?
<n>7:13</n> Except you will be converted, he will brandish his sword: * he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.
<n>7:14</n> And in it he hath prepared the instruments of death, * he hath made ready his arrows for them that burn.
<n>7:15</n> Behold he hath been in labour with injustice; * he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.
<n>7:16</n> He hath opened a pit and dug it: * and he is fallen into the hole he made.
<n>7:17</n> His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: * and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown.
<n>7:18</n> I will give glory to the Lord according to his justice: * and will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.
00.E8:
<n>8:3</n> Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.
<n>8:4</n> For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.
<n>8:5</n> What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?
<n>8:6</n> Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, † thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * (7) and hast set him over the works of thy hands.
<n>8:8</n> Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.
<n>8:9</n> The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.
<n>8:10</n> O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!
00.E9:
<n>9:2</n> I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: * I will relate all thy wonders.
<n>9:3</n> I will be glad and rejoice in thee: * I will sing to thy name, O thou most high.
<n>9:4</n> When my enemy shall be turned back: * they shall be weakened and perish before thy face.
<n>9:5</n> For thou hast maintained my judgment and my cause: * thou hast sat on the throne, who judgest justice.
<n>9:6</n> Thou hast rebuked the Gentiles, and the wicked one hath perished: * thou hast blotted out their name for ever and ever.
<n>9:10</n> And the Lord is become a refuge for the poor: * a helper in due time in tribulation.
<n>9:11</n> And let them trust in thee who know thy name: * for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee, O Lord.
<n>9:12</n> Sing ye to the Lord, who dwelleth in Sion: * declare his ways among the Gentiles.
<n>9:13</n> For requiring their blood he hath remembered them: * he hath not forgotten the cry of the poor.
<n>9:14</n> Have mercy on me, O Lord: * see my humiliation which I suffer from my enemies.
<n>9:15</n> Thou that liftest me up from the gates of death, * that I may declare all thy praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion.
<n>9:17</n> The Lord shall be known when he executeth judgments: * the sinner hath been caught in the works of his own hands.
<n>9:18</n> The wicked shall be turned into hell, * all the nations that forget God.
<n>9:19</n> For the poor man shall not be forgotten to the end: * the patience of the poor shall not perish for ever.
<n>9:20</n> Arise, O Lord, let not man be strengthened: * let the Gentiles be judged in thy sight.
<n>9:21</n> Appoint, O Lord, a lawgiver over them: * that the Gentiles may know themselves to be but men.
<n>9:22</n> Why, O Lord, hast thou retired afar off? * why dost thou slight us in our wants, in the time of trouble?
<n>9:23</n> Whilst the wicked man is proud, the poor is set on fire: * they are caught in the counsels which they devise.
<n>9:24</n> For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul: * and the unjust man is blessed.
<n>9:25</n> The sinner hath provoked the Lord, * according to the multitude of his wrath he will not seek him.
<n>9:27</n> For he hath said in his heart: * I shall not be moved from generation to generation, and shall be without evil.
<n>9:28</n> His mouth is full of cursing, and of bitterness, and of deceit: * under his tongue are labour and sorrow.
<n>9:29</n> He sitteth in ambush with the rich, in private places, * that he may kill the innocent.
<n>9:31</n> In his net he will bring him down, * he will crouch and fall, when he shall have power over the poor.
<n>9:32</n> For he hath said in his heart: God hath forgotten, * he hath turned away his face, not to see to the end.
<n>9:33</n> Arise, O Lord God, let thy hand be exalted: * forget not the poor.
<n>9:34</n> Wherefore hath the wicked provoked God? * for he hath said in his heart: He will not require it.
<n>9:36</n> Break thou the arm of the sinner and of the malignant: * his sin shall be sought, and shall not be found.
<n>9:37</n> The Lord shall reign to eternity, yea, for ever and ever: * ye Gentiles shall perish from his land.
<n>9:38</n> The Lord hath heard the desire of the poor: * thy ear hath heard the preparation of their heart.
<n>9:39</n> To judge for the fatherless and for the humble, * that man may no more presume to magnify himself upon earth.
00.L4:
<n>4:3</n> Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
<n>4:4</n> Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
<n>4:5</n> Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, * in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
<n>4:6</n> Sacrificáte sacrifícium justítiæ, † et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
<n>4:7</n> Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
<n>4:8</n> A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
<n>4:9</n> In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
<n>4:10</n> Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
00.E4:
<n>4:3</n> O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?
<n>4:4</n> Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.
<n>4:5</n> Be ye angry, and sin not: the things you say in your hearts, * be sorry for them upon your beds.
<n>4:6</n> Offer up the sacrifice of justice, † and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?
<n>4:7</n> The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.
<n>4:8</n> By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.
<n>4:9</n> In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:
<n>4:10</n> For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.
00.L5:
<n>5:2</n> Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.
<n>5:3</n> Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.
<n>5:4</n> Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.
<n>5:5</n> Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.
<n>5:6</n> Neque habitábit juxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt injústi ante óculos tuos.
<n>5:9</n> Dómine, deduc me in justítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
<n>5:10</n> Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.
00.E5:
<n>5:2</n> Give ear, O Lord, to my words * understand my cry.
<n>5:3</n> Hearken to the voice of my prayer, * O my King and my God.
<n>5:4</n> For to thee will I pray: * O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.
<n>5:5</n> In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: * because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.
<n>5:6</n> Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: * nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.
<n>5:9</n> Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: * because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.
<n>5:10</n> For there is no truth in their mouth: * their heart is vain.
